subject: Genetics
title: Insertions and Deletions
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Insertions and Deletions.

hook.text: Add one letter to a sentence and every word after it shifts. In DNA, that's a frameshift—and it's devastating.

buildup.text: DNA is read in triplets. Insert or delete one base, and every codon downstream is misread. Total protein chaos.

discovery.text: Cystic fibrosis is caused by a 3-base deletion in the CFTR gene. Just three missing letters. One missing amino acid.

twist.text: Insertions of three bases add an amino acid without disrupting the frame. The sentence stays readable.

climax.text: The reading frame is sacred. Disrupt it and the protein is gibberish. Preserve it and changes may be survivable.

punchline.text: Three letters missing. One protein broken. One disease.

quiz.question: Why are single-base insertions so damaging?
options: They shift the reading frame of all downstream codons
